entries.plain: Copies in another file of declarations before your program is compiled. stdio.h provides printf.
The function where every C program starts. Returning 0 means the program finished successfully.
Prints formatted text to the screen. Use %d for a whole number, %f for a decimal, and %s for text.
Reads formatted input from the keyboard. Pass the address of a variable with & so scanf can fill it in.
Leaves the current function and optionally sends a value back to whoever called it.
A whole-number type, such as 3 or -12.
A single character type. A char array is often used for text in C.
A number type that can hold a decimal point. double stores more precision.
Runs the following block only when a condition is true.
Runs when the matching if condition was false.
Repeats a block. The three parts set up a counter, test it, and change it after each pass.
Repeats a block while a condition stays true.
Several values of the same type stored together. Indexes start at 0.
Groups several related values under one type name.
A value that stores the memory address of something else. The * symbol declares or follows a pointer.
Asks the system for a block of memory at runtime. Release it with free() when you are done.
